about: Stages and timing for the category-tune-up playbook. scripts/handoff.py reads this file: the stages it tracks, the outcomes each stage can record, and how long to wait between stages. Each key is explained under notes.

stages.name: health
stages.do: Check category pages against like-for-like peers, empty dynamic categories, category rules and buried products, and add the fixes as findings.

stages.name: dynamic
stages.do: Review every dynamic category's definition, size, overlaps and performance, and add the fixes as findings for the dashboard.

stages.name: suggest
stages.do: Suggest new collections shoppers want but can't browse to, with a rule and a live preview each, and agree which to build.

stages.name: build
stages.do: Build the chosen collection in depth: products scored for how strongly they belong, rule-based definitions tested for what they wrongly include and miss, and the dashboard steps.

skip_when.reason: no new collection was worth building.

stages.name: measure
stages.do: Check the category or dynamic category the user changed in the dashboard paid off, with the change and its live date from the hand-off file.

skip_when.reason: no stage found anything to change, so there is nothing to measure.

notes.measure_after_days: Days before the measure stage is due. The script counts them from the health stage, as a floor; when the user reports a dashboard change, the run also sets the measure stage's date from the day it went live, which is the date that matters. change-impact-tracker needs about 14 days of data after a change for a verdict other than too early to tell.
notes.max_chosen: How many findings can be chosen at once: the category and dynamic category fixes the user agrees to make in the dashboard, and the collection to build.
notes.wait_outcomes: Outcomes that mean a stage isn't finished yet. The script records them only with status in_progress and a --not-before date to come back on, so status never shows the stage as due before then.
notes.playbooks: Each playbook's title, product and stages in order. A stage names the skill that does it, whether that skill writes, what to do, the outcomes it can record, not_before (wait this rules key's number of days after another stage is done) and skip_when (suggest skipping when an earlier stage had one of these outcomes; all means every condition must hold). Every stage skill is read-only: the user makes the changes in the Discovery dashboard, and the run records them so the measure stage and playbook-quarter-close see them.
